answer:
Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) with mshr for geometry and mesh generation.
The domain is a rectangular strip Ω = (0, 1.0) × (0, 0.20) m with two circular holes of radius 0.04 m centred at (0.40, 0.10) m and (0.60, 0.10) m.
Generate the mesh with maximum cell size 0.01 m using mshr.
Use a mixed displacement–pressure finite element pair: displacement u in P2 (VectorElement Lagrange degree 2 on triangle) and pressure p in P1 (ScalarElement Lagrange degree 1 on triangle).
The material is an isotropic quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean solid under plane strain, with strain energy W = (μ/2)(I₁ − 3) + (1/(2λ))(J − 1)², where μ = E/(2(1+ν)) and λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)).
Set Young's modulus E = 5 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.49.
Boundary conditions: on the left edge (x = 0) fix u_x = 0 and u_y = 0; on the right edge (x = 1.0) prescribe u_x = 0.060 m and u_y = 0; on the top and bottom edges apply zero traction; on each hole boundary apply a follower pressure P_hole = 0.10 MPa.
The follower pressure traction on each hole boundary is t = P_hole · n_deformed, where n_deformed = (Fᵀ · n_ref)/|Fᵀ · n_ref|, F is the deformation gradient, and n_ref is the outward mesh normal of the undeformed hole boundary. Do not use the reference normal directly.
Solve the resulting nonlinear system with Newton's method using dolfin's NewtonSolver.
After convergence, compute the Cauchy stress σ = J⁻¹ P (where P is the first Piola–Kirchhoff stress) and derive the von Mises stress from σ.
Save a colour map of the hydrostatic pressure p as q14_p.png.
Save a colour map of the von Mises stress as q14_vm.png.
Save the converged displacement field in XDMF format.
